submissions.title: NVIDIA Guarantees SB Energy's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio to Exclusively Host NVIDIA AI Compute
submissions.excerpt: Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion in conditional lease and power payment obligations to SB Energy
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT. OpenAI signed a 20-year lease with SB Energy (SoftBank-backed) for capacity at the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant site (PORTS-Pike) in Pike County, Ohio. SB Energy/SoftBank plan >=10 GW of new power generation yielding 8 IT-GW of AI factory capacity; initial deployment is 4.25 IT-GW committed to OpenAI, with NVIDIA holding an option on the remaining 3.75 IT-GW. First 800 MW targeted online 2028 using existing AEP infrastructure; full buildout through 2032. NVIDIA is also investing $1.5B directly in SB Energy and is the exclusive compute vendor. IMPORTANT: the $105B figure is a lease/power-payment guarantee (per an SEC filing), NOT capex — deliberately omitted as a CAPEX_USD claim per project data rules. Distinct site from the already-tracked Stargate Lordstown, Ohio (Trumbull County) project — no overlap. submissions.title: Governor Shapiro Signs Executive Order on Data Center Development in PA
submissions.excerpt: prohibits any state agency from signing a nondisclosure agreement related to a data center project
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Governor Shapiro signed Executive Order 2026-05 (Aug 18, 2026), a statewide policy applying to all Commonwealth agencies, not a single project. It directs DEP to evaluate data center permit applications only where the developer has made a legally binding commitment to the Governor's 'Responsible Infrastructure Development' (GRID) requirements AND received local approval; removes AI data center proposals from the state's Fast Track permitting process; and bars state NDAs on data center projects. Context per PA officials: of ~100 pending PA data center proposals, only 5 have obtained permits, and most are described as speculative/under-financed. No specific tracked PA project is directly named in coverage reviewed. submissions.title: Meta can keep its data center details private, PSC decides
submissions.excerpt: commissioners voted 3-1 to overrule the judge's order requiring Meta to disclose its job and power-need calculations
submissions.note: Regulatory/transparency development on tracked project Meta Hyperion (Richland Parish, LA). On Aug 12, 2026 the Louisiana Public Service Commission voted 3-1 along party lines (Coussan, Francis, Skrmetta vs. Lewis; Campbell absent) to overrule its own administrative law judge, who had ordered Meta to disclose how it calculated the job and power-demand figures underlying Entergy's turbine-build applications for Hyperion. Petitioners were the Alliance for Affordable Energy, Union of Concerned Scientists, and Sierra Club; Meta cited trade-secret protection. This does NOT change Hyperion's tracked MW/capex figures (already recorded: 5,000 MW / $50B target, UNDER_CONSTRUCTION) — it is an oversight/disclosure ruling, logged here because it affects how future power-need claims for this project can be independently verified. submissions.title: Data center moratorium takes first steps after Fort Worth City Council's unanimous vote
submissions.excerpt: council voted unanimously to begin the process for a 90-day moratorium on new data center construction
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Fort Worth (TX) City Council voted unanimously on Aug 11, 2026 to begin the formal process toward a 90-day construction moratorium on new data centers, to allow the city to evaluate development regulations and impacts on resources/quality of life. This is a first procedural step, not yet an enacted moratorium — reporting points to a possible effective date around Feb 16, 2027, with zoning applications filed before then reportedly exempted. Not tied to a specific tracked project. submissions.title: Louisville Metro Council approves data center moratorium as new proposal sparks controversy
submissions.excerpt: passed on a 24 to 1 vote, preventing new data center proposals from being approved for six months
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Louisville Metro Council (Jefferson County, KY) passed a 6-month moratorium on approving new data center proposals, 24-1, on Aug 13, 2026 (or until comprehensive zoning rules are adopted). A companion framework under discussion would ban hyperscale data centers over 500,000 sq ft in Jefferson County outright and impose buffer/setback and utility-rate-protection requirements on smaller facilities reusing existing buildings. Prompted partly by a developer's plan to convert a 350,000-sq-ft warehouse into a data center. Not tied to a specific tracked project.
